meta.title_plain: How a chatbot answers you one word at a time
meta.teaser: Tokens, trillions of words and one big guessing game: how AI chatbots talk.

page.title: How a chatbot answers you one word at a time
page.bigIdea: A chatbot like Claude is a giant guessing machine. It learned from huge amounts of text to predict the next word, again and again.

cards.title: Your message becomes tokens
cards.front: Chatbots don't read words the way you do.
cards.back: First, your text is chopped into tokens: small chunks, usually a few letters long. Each token becomes a list of numbers the computer can work with.
cards.tryit: Split the word "unbelievable" into three chunks a chatbot might use. Then try "Fortnite" and "tennis".

cards.title: Practice on a giant library
cards.front: Before it can chat, it has to train. A lot.
cards.back: The model studies trillions of tokens of text. Its training game is simple: guess the next word, check, and adjust. Like serving again and again until it lands.
cards.tryit: Ask someone to read a sentence from a book and stop halfway. Guess the next word. How often are you right?

cards.title: Patterns, not memories
cards.front: It doesn't store answers like a dictionary.
cards.back: It learns which words usually follow others. "The cat sat on the mat" sounds likely. "Sat the the mat cat on" doesn't. These patterns live in billions of settings called parameters.
cards.tryit: Write three sentence starts, like "In Roblox you can..." Then write the ending you think most people would choose.

cards.title: Coached to be a helper
cards.front: A raw model just keeps writing. That's not a chat.
cards.back: So it gets extra training, called fine-tuning, on example conversations. That teaches it to follow instructions and answer like an assistant. Think of a coach fixing your forehand.
cards.tryit: Think of one tip a coach gave you that changed your game. Write it down in one sentence.

cards.title: Why it still makes mistakes
cards.front: Chatbots can sound sure and still be wrong.
cards.back: It picks words that sound likely, not facts it has checked. So it can make up wrong facts confidently. Experts call this a hallucination. Always double-check important facts.
cards.tryit: With Dad, ask a chatbot about something you know really well. Can you spot anything it gets wrong?

quiz.q: What happens to your message first?
opts: It is sent to a person
quiz.hint: Think about chopping a sentence into small pieces.
quiz.why: The chatbot splits your text into tokens and turns each one into numbers.

quiz.q: What is the main game a model plays in training?
quiz.why: It practises predicting the next word over and over, adjusting after every guess.

quiz.q: Why can a chatbot be confidently wrong?
opts: It picks likely-sounding words, not checked facts
quiz.hint: Does sounding right mean being right?
quiz.why: It chooses words that fit the pattern, so a false sentence can still sound smooth and sure.

opts: Teaches it to act like a helpful assistant
quiz.why: Fine-tuning on example conversations teaches the model to follow instructions and chat.

page.think: Imagine a chatbot trained only on One Piece episodes and tennis matches. What would it be great at? What silly mistakes might it make if you asked it about homework or cooking?
